Front: Grounding vs model tuning - what does each improve?
Back: Grounding improves FACTUALITY/currency: connect the model to trusted external data so answers are verified against latest info (implemented via RAG; in Agent Studio ground via Google Search or your own data). Model tuning improves the GENERATION itself (style/format/task quality) by changing the model. Grounding first (cheap, updatable); tune only if generation quality is the gap.

Front: Three model-tuning approaches and what each changes?
Back: Prompt design: examples/instructions in natural language, does NOT alter pretrained weights. Parameter-efficient/adapter tuning: updates a SMALL subset (added adapter weights), adapts a large model to your task. Full fine-tuning: updates ALL parameters, complex tasks, high compute. Agent Studio/Agent Platform supports supervised fine-tuning (labeled data: classification, summarization, extraction, chat).

Front: Decoding params: temperature vs top-k vs top-p?
Back: Temperature = randomness (low = narrow to high-probability/focused; high = include low-probability/creative). Top-k = sample from the k most-probable tokens (fixed count). Top-p/nucleus = smallest token set whose cumulative probability >= p, sample from it (dynamic count).

Front: The three components of an AI agent + the body analogy?
Back: Model = reasoning (brain), can be one OR multiple foundation models. Tools = external interaction (hands/senses). Orchestration = coordination (nervous system). Goal-oriented: the orchestration layer coordinates models + tools to reach a desired goal.

Front: GCP agent-build spectrum by amount of code (4 levels)?
Back: Level 4 solutions (no code): Gemini Enterprise App, Gemini Enterprise for CX. Level 3: Agent Platform / Agent Studio / Agent Garden (customizable, no/low code); ADK = pro-code custom dev. Level 2: low-level orchestration framework (e.g. LangGraph). Level 1: build your own via function calling.

Front: Three parts of the Agent Platform and what each does?
Back: Agent Studio: low-code visual interface to design agent reasoning loops + test prompts in natural language. ADK: graph-based logic for networks of sub-agents; agent-to-agent delegation with generative + deterministic patterns. Agent Runtime: deploy/manage/scale agents in prod (sub-second cold starts, long-running workflows, integrated observability).

Front: Gemini Enterprise App vs Gemini Enterprise for CX?
Back: Gemini Enterprise App = internal hub: cited answers across all org data formats (docs/images/video) in one interface, plus a hub for agents (pre-built Google agents + no-code Agent Designer) that update tickets, send email, analyze reports. Gemini Enterprise for CX = customer-facing experience agents for industries like retail.

Front: General vs specialty foundation models on GCP + 'horizontal AI'?
Back: General: Gemini (Pro/Flash/Flash-Lite). Specialty: Nano Banana (images), Veo (video), Embeddings. Foundation models are 'horizontal AI' (broad capabilities from pretraining on vast data), then fine-tuned for a specific use case. Parameter count (millions -> trillions) roughly indicates capacity.

Front: The three sections of the Agent Studio UI?
Back: System instructions: processed before prompts, apply to the whole request across user/model turns. Model settings: pick model (incl. 3rd-party), configure parameters, enable tools (e.g. grounding), advanced options. Prompt: draft the (multimodal) prompt.
